title: Pokémon GO Started as a Google Maps April Fools' Joke
hook: On March 31, 2014 Google Maps hid wild Pokémon across its real map as a prank. The engineer behind it went on to help build Pokémon GO. Did you catch anything in Google Maps back then?
script: Did you know Pokemon Go started as an April Fools joke? On the last day of March in twenty fourteen, Google Maps hid wild Pokemon all over its real world map. The post came from a Google engineer named Tatsuo Nomura, and The Pokemon Company gave its blessing. Anyone with the Maps app could tap the search bar, press start, and catch Pokemon on streets and mountains around the globe. Google said whoever caught them all could become a Pokemon Master, and the winners received a business card with that title. The video went viral, and the idea was too good to stay a prank. The Pokemon Company's president got talking with John Hanke, who ran Niantic, the Google team behind the location game Ingress. Nomura left Maps to join Niantic and help build the real thing. Niantic spun out of Google the following year, and Pokemon Go finally launched in early July of twenty sixteen. The servers buckled almost immediately, because traffic ran about fifty times higher than planned. The game is still going a decade later. This week it announced a crossover with the battle game Pokemon Champions that starts on December eighth. Did you catch anything in Google Maps back when it was a prank? Follow for more gaming history.
